quarterly_data.signal: CEO repeated the AI data center dollar sizing and put a definition around it: 'The doubling is happening from last year's $250 million to this year to over $500 million,' and he defined AI data center revenue as revenue generated inside the walls of the data center only - energy storage systems stay in industrial even though AI drives them. Growth came across the whole power tree, not one stage: 'The strength that we saw in the second quarter was actually across all of our content, not one piece did better than the other.' Platforms and customers named behind it: Flex Power, Delta, Lite-On, Great Wall, AWS, Nvidia.
quarterly_data.figure: AI data center revenue from $250 million last year to over $500 million this year

quarterly_data.signal: CFO laid out the full gross-margin bridge: utilization was 68% exiting last year and 83% last quarter, with fully utilized at 92%-93%; 'Every point of utilization is 25 to 30 basis points of gross margin improvement just two quarters later.' Q2 carried 650 basis points of underutilization charges, so closing the gap to 92-93 is 650 basis points of tailwind. On top of that: FabRight about 200 basis points (50 of it from the two manufacturing sites divested last quarter, some layering in 2027 and most in 2028), favourable mix from differentiated products about 200 basis points, and burning the bridge inventory built for the earlier fab divestitures another 200 basis points. He expects further gross margin improvement in Q4 and into next year.
quarterly_data.figure: utilization 68% exiting last year -> 83% last quarter, fully utilized 92%-93%; 25 to 30 basis points per point; 650 basis points Q2 underutilization; FabRight 200 basis points (50 from two site divestitures); mix 200 basis points; bridge inventory 200 basis points

quarterly_data.signal: CEO explained the mechanics behind prioritizing AI data center over auto/industrial and put a clock on it: capacity is fungible from the fab all the way through technology (the same 1,200 volt silicon carbide serves automotive and 800 volt AI data center systems) until roughly 2 weeks from finished goods when the die gets its marketing part number - 'Compare that 2-week change in end product to a little over 30 weeks of lead time.' New wafers for the auto and industrial orders take about 3 to 6 months to come out, so the trade-off 'will normalize in the next couple of quarters.' Capacity itself is not the constraint: 'We are not fully utilized... It is not like we cannot do the capacity and we need more CapEx. Our CapEx remains unchanged. CapEx remains mid-single digit,' and the company can flex outside even at 92%-93%.
quarterly_data.figure: fungible until ~2 weeks from finished goods vs a little over 30 weeks lead time; new wafers out in 3 to 6 months; normalizes in the next couple of quarters; CapEx stays mid-single digit

quarterly_data.signal: Vertical GaN status: the high-voltage part is a monolithic 1,200 volts single die - 'non-stacked die' - and has been sampled both in AI data centers and in automotive. 'Quals are progressing as expected, and the fab is-- We build in our own fab. All of the big hurdles that I would say is, can you manufacture it? Is it yielding? Does it qual? Is it performing? All of these are check the box.'
quarterly_data.figure: monolithic 1,200 volts single-die vertical GaN sampled in AI data center and automotive

quarterly_data.signal: A channel shift the earnings call did not describe: automotive OEMs are bypassing tier ones and ordering directly from onsemi, because tier-one balance sheets cannot carry inventory. 'They're buying directly from us... We ship to the OEM. When the OEM has the demand, they decide which tier one gets it. They're doing the allocation.' Today that is mostly Chinese OEMs and North American EV makers rather than traditional automakers, and CEO warned that with no automotive replenishment cycle yet, 'when demand does pick up in automotive with no replenishment, the constraint that we're seeing today will get even worse.'
